newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malaysian-backed black group plans S.Africa resort.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian-backed black group plans S.Africa resort.

text.p: South Africa's Magic Kingdom Holdings, a mainly black investment group, and Malaysia's Genting International said on Thursday they aimed to build a new entertainment and retail development in the central Pretoria.

The project, dubbed City Lake, will involve the creation of a central city lake bordered by an international hotel and casino resort and a shopping complex. No financial details of the scheme were announced.
Magic Kingdom chief executive Fred Ndlovu said Pretoria was a fast growing city and needed facilities to cope with incoming migrants.

"Our project represents one of the most innovative and viable developments which will provide Pretoria with a means to cope with many migrant families now establishing their homes in and around the city," he said.
The project also forms the centre-piece of the group's bid for a casino licence in South Africa's populous and heavily industrialised Gauteng province.

The country's newly liberalised gaming laws have prompted a flood of licence bids as companies hope to cash in on South African's desire to take a flutter after decades of apartheid era discouragement of gaming.

Genting International is part of Genting Berhad and has diverse interests from leisure and entertainment to pulp and paper. Genting will hold a 50 percent stake in the City Lake project and be the principal financier to the development.

"Genting will bring not only the management expertise needed to run such an international operation, but will be making a considerble contribution to the South African economy as a foreign investor," Magic Kingdom said in a statement.
Genting said that if the project proved a money spinner it would consider investing elsewhere in the country, joining a rash of Malaysian firms that have moved into post-apartheid South Africa.

"If we see that City Lake delivers the return on investment we believe it can do, then Genting will definitely consider investing in other areas of the South African economy," Genting executive director Colin Au said.
Magic Kingdom is 45 percent owned by black investment consortium Inotho.
